blocks.passage:
A good business presentation is not a report read out loud. It is a guided journey, built around a clear message that the audience should remember one week later.

Start by deciding that message — the one sentence the audience must walk away with. Everything else supports it. If a slide does not support the message, it should not be in the deck, however pretty it looks.

Delivery matters as much as content. Pause more than you think you should. Look at individuals, not at the screen. And remember: you already know the material better than anyone in the room. Your job is not to prove you are smart — it is to make the audience smarter about this topic.

items.q: According to the text, a good presentation is…
options: a guided journey built around a clear message
items.why: "It is a guided journey, built around a clear message."

items.q: What should you decide first?
options: The one sentence the audience must walk away with
items.why: "Start by deciding that message — the one sentence the audience must walk away with."

items.q: What should happen to a slide that doesn't support the message?
options: Keep it if it looks good
Remove it, however pretty it looks
items.why: "If a slide does not support the message, it should not be in the deck, however pretty it looks."

items.q: What does the text advise about delivery?
options: Pause more than you think, and look at individuals
items.why: "Pause more than you think you should. Look at individuals, not at the screen."

items.q: "Your job is not to prove you are smart — it is to make the audience smarter." This suggests the focus should be on…
items.why: Inferência: o foco é o aprendizado da plateia, não a imagem do apresentador.

audio.text:
Okay, let me run you through the pitch before we take it to the client. I've been tightening it all morning.

The key message is one line: "We can cut your delivery time by a third without raising costs." Everything in the deck now points to that. If a slide doesn't, it's gone.

I've actually removed three slides. The company-history slide was nice, but it didn't support the message, so out it went. However good it looked, it was slowing the story down.

On delivery, I'm going to pause after the key number instead of rushing on. Last time I spoke too fast and the number just disappeared. This time I'll let it land.

And I'll look at people, not the screen. The content is strong; I just need to guide them through it, one clear step at a time, and leave five minutes for Q&A at the end.

items.q: What is the key message of James's pitch?
options: Delivery time can be cut by a third without raising costs
The product is the cheapest available
The company has a long history
items.why: "We can cut your delivery time by a third without raising costs."

items.q: Why did James remove the company-history slide?
options: It didn't support the key message
The client had seen it before
items.why: "it didn't support the message, so out it went."

items.q: What will James do differently after saying the key number?
options: Put it on a new slide
items.why: "I'm going to pause after the key number instead of rushing on… I'll let it land."

items.q: What went wrong last time, according to James?
options: He spoke too fast and the number disappeared
items.why: "Last time I spoke too fast and the number just disappeared."

items.q: What does James plan to leave time for at the end?
items.why: "leave five minutes for Q&A at the end."

items.q: "She's ready to **pitch** the idea to the board." To pitch means to…
items.why: To pitch = apresentar e defender uma ideia.

items.q: The **key message** of a presentation is…
options: the one idea the audience must remember
items.why: Key message = mensagem-chave, a ideia central.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He'll **rehearse** the talk twice before the meeting." To rehearse means to…
items.why: To rehearse = ensaiar.

items.q: A **deck** in business English is…
items.why: Deck = o conjunto de slides.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Let's keep the **storyline** simple — one point per slide." Storyline means…
options: the line of reasoning through the talk
items.why: Storyline = a linha de raciocínio da apresentação.

items.q: "Let me **walk you through** the numbers." To walk someone through means to…
items.why: Walk through = conduzir passo a passo.

items.q: "I'll **kick off** with the main finding." To kick off means to…
items.why: Kick off = começar.

items.q: "Let's **wrap up** with the three takeaways." To wrap up means to…
items.why: Wrap up = concluir.

items.q: "That slide doesn't **land**, so I'll cut it." If a point lands, it…
options: has a clear effect on the audience
items.why: To land = surtir efeito, ser bem recebido.

items.q: "We'll **open the floor** for questions at the end." To open the floor means to…
options: invite the audience to speak or ask
items.why: Open the floor = abrir para perguntas/participação.
